newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says plans to offer 20-year bonds.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says plans to offer 20-year bonds.

text.p: The Philippines plans to introduce 20-year bonds in the local market in the next six months, national treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa said on Monday.
Valdehuesa said the Bureau of Treasury plans to sell initially two billion pesos worth of 20-year bonds.
"There is a demand for longer-term securities because the Philippine economy is not only stabilizing but actually growing," Valdehuesa said.
Bureau of Treasury director Roberto Juanchito Dispo said President Fidel Ramos has approved the issuance of the 20-year bonds.
He said the Bureau of Treasury was discussing issue of the bonds with accredited government securities dealers.
But bankers seemed cool to the government's plan to float 20-year bonds.

"We have to make sure that all necessary structures are in place before introducing longer-term bonds," said an official of the Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) who requested not to be named.

The official said the government has to set up incentives to lure investors to buy longer-term bonds. He said he expected a "limited" market for such type of securities because only firms which can ensure long term liquidity such as insurance companies can invest their money for a long period.
The government also has to resolve a lot of taxation and infrastructure problems to create a better market for these securities, he said without elaborating.
